newsitem.title: USA: Excel "in better shape" to deal with market.
newsitem.headline: Excel "in better shape" to deal with market.

text.p: Excel Industries Inc said Wednesday that the integration of an acquired company and the sale of its automotive parking brake business improved the company's ability to deal with softening in the market.
"Our markets exhibit some softening tendencies, but we are in better shape to respond," James Futterknecht, chief executive, said in a statement.

During the second quarter, Excel said it made substantial progress in integrating Anderson Industries' Atwood unit into Excel's operations. The company also completed the sale of its parking brake division.
In addition, the shutdown and sale of its Rockford, Ill. automotive plant is nearly complete, and the shutdown of the Battle Creek, Michigan plant will likely be concluded in the third quarter.
Excel reported second quarter earnings of $0.85 per primary share versus $0.75 last year. Sales fell four percent to $274.148 million.
Excel produces windows, doors and seats, among other things, for the automotive, truck and bus industry.
